node.title: Re: substr odd behavior with list arguments
node.author: choroba
node.doctext:
That's because prototype(\&CORE::substr) is $$;$$. It means each argument is evaluated in scalar context, so in the second case @a is interpreted as scalar @a, i.e. the size of the array, which is 2.

Use my ($offset, $length) = a_subroutine_call_that_returns_offset_and_length(@some_args); substr('abcdefg', $offset, $length);
